'''Norman Herbert Anning''' ({{birth date|1883|8|28|mf=yes}} – {{Death date|1963|05|1|mf=yes}}) was an American mathematician and academic. He is known for a proof of the characterization of [[infinite set]]s of points in the plane with mutually [[integer]] distances, known as the [[Erdős–Anning theorem]].

==Life==

Anning was originally from Holland Township (currently [[Chatsworth, Ontario|Chatsworth]]), [[Grey County]], [[Ontario]], Canada. In 1902, he won a scholarship to [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]],<ref name=anning/> and received the Arts bachelor's degree in 1905, and the Arts master's degree in 1906 from the same institution.<ref name=anning/>

==Academic career==
Anning served in the faculty of the [[University of Michigan]] since 1920, until he retired on 1953.<ref name=anning>{{cite web |url=http://um2017.org/faculty-history/faculty/norman-herbert-anning/memorial |title=University of Michigan Faculty History Project |last1=Copeland |first1=Arthur Herbert |last2=Hay |first2=George E }}</ref><ref name=project>{{cite web |url=http://um2017.org/faculty-history/faculty/norman-herbert-anning |title=Norman Herbert Anning – University of Michigan Faculty History Project |accessdate=25 January 2017}}</ref>

From 1909 to 1910, he held a teaching position in the department of Mathematics and Science at [[Chilliwack Secondary School|Chilliwack High School]], British Columbia.<ref name=anning/> Anning was appointed as chairperson at the [[University of Michigan]] from 1951 to 1952,<ref name=naa>{{cite web |title=Mathematical Association of America – Michigan Section |author=Yousef Alavi |year=2005 |url=http://sections.maa.org/michigan/history.html |accessdate=25 January 2017}}</ref> and treasurer secretary from 1925 to 1926 at the same institution.<ref name=naa />

{{Quote box |quote=The name of Norman Anning must certainly be familiar to every contributor to this department. He has been solving problems for this department for more years than its present editor has known of ''School Science and Mathematics''. |source=Charles H. Smith, editor of ''School Science and Mathematics'' |width=60% |align=right }}

With [[Paul Erdős]], he published a paper in 1945 containing what is now known as the [[Erdős–Anning theorem]]. The theorem states that an infinite number of points in the plane can have mutual integer distances only if all the points lie on a straight line.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Integral distances |last1=Anning |first1=Norman H. |last2=Erdos |first2=Paul |journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |year=1945 |volume=51 |issue=8 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1945-51-08/S0002-9904-1945-08407-9/S0002-9904-1945-08407-9.pdf |pages=598–00 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1945-08407-9 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Anning retired on August 28, 1953. He died in [[Sunnydale, California]] on May 1, 1963.<ref name=anning/>
